COLORS LESSON · COLORS & SHADES · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Green — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the color green: the color of leaves, frogs and lunchbox vegetables.

What is this?

Green is a color — the color of the leaf, the frog, the cucumber and the turtle on the card. It is the color of growing things: nearly every plant wears green while it grows.

What does it mean?

Green is the go-and-grow color: traffic lights say GO in green, gardens grow in green, frogs hop in green. Your child is learning the color of alive-and-happening.

What does the child need to know?

The child needs to: say "green", notice green outside (leaves, grass), and meet green on an animal (frog), a plant part (leaf), a vegetable (cucumber) and a reptile (turtle).

Why this matters

Green is the color children meet OUTSIDE more than inside — this card is the bridge from kitchen-table colors to park-walk colors.

What it teaches

Vocabulary, indoor-outdoor transfer (the card&rsquo;s green matches the real grass), and movement anchoring — hopping while saying the word wires it deep.

Words to learn

greenleaffrogcucumberturtlehopgrowcrunchslowshell

Say this to your child

“"Green! The leaf is green, the frog is green, the cucumber is green, the turtle is green. Green is the color of growing things. Hop like a frog — fast! Now slow like a turtle… slooow…"”

Step by step

  1. Point and name: leaf — green, frog — green, cucumber — green, turtle — green. Hop once per square; the frog square earns three.
  2. The leaf question: "what does a leaf do before it turns brown?" It grows — green is the GROWING color. Any plant near the window is proof; go visit it.
  3. The crunch test: cucumber at snack time, word said first, crunch counted after. If cucumbers are outlawed in your house, any green vegetable drafts in.
  4. Speed game: frog hops FAST, turtle crawls SLOW — race both across the rug. The turtle always wins the slow race.
  5. Close at the window or garden: find the biggest green thing you can see together. Name it green, and name it yours.

Look closer at the picture

Two squares are animals in green suits (frog, turtle), two are plants and plant-food (leaf, cucumber). Green is the only color on the shelf worn by a whole kingdom — the plant one.

Ask your child

"Which green thing hops?" (frog) "Which green thing hides in its shell?" (turtle) "Which green thing do we crunch at snack time?" (cucumber)

What your child can say or do

Your child might croak at every green light, or announce the lawn is "a hundred leaves". Green pride is real — let it hop.

Out in the real world

Green means GO at crossings in the US, UK and Canada — a park-walk green light is this card waving hello. Frogs, turtles and cucumbers are green nearly everywhere on Earth.

Try it together

Frog hop path: cut five paper leaves, lay a trail, and hop leaf to leaf saying "green" per hop. The turtle finish (slow crawl to the couch) is the cool-down.

Understanding check

Ask: "what color is the frog?" (green) "What grows green outside?" (grass, leaves — whatever the window shows) "Is the turtle fast or slow?" (slow — with the matching crawl)

This lesson pairs with the Green flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Colors & Shades.
